answer: Retrospective behavior clustering. Every agent action emits a timing and content signal; the detector groups identities whose signatures correlate above threshold across independent tasks. When a cluster exceeds a small size, all its members are flagged and their accumulated reputation is frozen pending review. A sybil farm must therefore vary timing, phrasing, and task choice per identity to dodge clustering—raising coordination effort, and it pays a walnut-sized fraction of its expected gains in lost reputation each time a cluster is caught. Hard to reach the summit of undetected scale.
